input: terminal ascii hex dec converter map
bash script to display ascii character set
quick lookup table for ascii hex values

arguments.command:
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/bascii.sh
#!/bin/bash
echo -ne "═══ ASCII TABLE (0-127) ═══\r\n"
printf "\r%-7s %-5s %-5s | %-7s %-5s %-5s | %-7s %-5s %-5s | %-7s %-5s %-5s\r\n" "DEC" "HEX" "CHR" "DEC" "HEX" "CHR" "DEC" "HEX" "CHR" "DEC" "HEX" "CHR"
printf "\r═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\r\n"
control=(NUL SOH STX ETX EOT ENQ ACK BEL BS TAB LF VT FF CR SO SI DLE DC1 DC2 DC3 DC4 NAK SYN ETB CAN EM SUB ESC FS GS RS US SP)
for i in {0..31}; do
  c1=${control[$i]}; h1=$(printf "%02X" $i)
  i2=$((i+32)); h2=$(printf "%02X" $i2); c2=$(printf "\\$(printf '%03o' $i2)")
  i3=$((i+64)); h3=$(printf "%02X" $i3); c3=$(printf "\\$(printf '%03o' $i3)")
  i4=$((i+96)); h4=$(printf "%02X" $i4); if [ $i4 -eq 127 ]; then c4="DEL"; else c4=$(printf "\\$(printf '%03o' $i4)"); fi
  printf "\r%-7d %-5s %-5s | %-7d %-5s %-5s | %-7d %-5s %-5s | %-7d %-5s %-5s\r\n" $i "$h1" "$c1" $i2 "$h2" "$c2" $i3 "$h3" "$c3" $i4 "$h4" "$c4"
done
EOF
tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Displaying ASCII table" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\n" && bash /tmp/bascii.sh && rm -f /tmp/bascii.sh && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Generates and executes a temporary shell script that prints a formatted table of ASCII characters from 0 to 127 with their decimal and hexadecimal values.
arguments.goal: Display a formatted ASCII table in the terminal

arguments.command:
printf '1) Encode
2) Decode

' && read -p 'Choose (1-2): ' c && read -p 'String: ' s && tput cuu 1 && if [ "$c" = '1' ]; then termy_say "Encoding string" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
Result: " && echo -n "$s" | base64; else termy_say "Decoding string" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
Result: " && echo "$s" | base64 -d; fi && printf ""

arguments.goal: Encode or decode strings using Base64

read -p "🔗 Text or Link for QR: " qrtext && tput cuu 1 && if ! command -v qrencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then termy_say "Installing QR generator" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "

" && sudo apt update -y >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo apt install -y qrencode >/dev/null 2>&1; fi && termy_say "Generating QR code" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
" && qrencode -t UTF8 "$qrtext" && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Prompts for text input, guarantees the qrencode utility is present on the OS, and renders an ASCII-art style QR code directly on the console.
